name: org.gcc.usp.modules.mydata.profile.ProfileController
comment: Feature mydata.profile (ME-01): proxies SAP's /sap/tamkeen/profile/me as the signed-in user; nothing is persisted.

methods.name: date
methods.comment: SAP sends dd-MM-yyyy (e.g. 23-09-2000); ISO is accepted too. Unparseable → null rather than failing the page.

name: org.gcc.usp.platform.config.ConfigController
comment: Versions of one configuration kind (leave, need, comms, designer…), for its policy center.

name: org.gcc.usp.platform.config.ConfigService
comment: The version machine shared by every versioned configuration (§7.10, the prototype's policy versions): draft → schedule (date, reason, reference) → optional second approval → in force on its date; correction, revert, rebase of stale drafts, change log and operations log. Managers and the second approver are SAP positions, read on the fly.

methods.name: versionOn
methods.comment: The version in force on a date (requests capture it at submission, D-009).

methods.name: diff
methods.comment: AB-91: difference between any two versions of a kind.

methods.name: newDraft
methods.comment: A new draft on the tip of the chain, or a correction: a copy of a version in force that replaces it from its own date.

methods.name: updateContent
methods.comment: Saves the draft's full content; the change log is recomputed against its base, keeping who/when/why of unchanged lines.

methods.name: setScope
methods.comment: Widens or changes what the draft may touch (null = everything).

methods.name: cancel
methods.comment: A draft, or a scheduled version before its date.

methods.name: approve
methods.comment: Second approval by the holder of the governance position — never the version's own author.

methods.name: returnToDraft
methods.comment: Returns the version to draft with a note for its author.

methods.name: revert
methods.comment: Takes back the active version; the one before it applies again. Refused once a request was evaluated under it.

methods.name: logOps
methods.comment: Operational changes (windows, groups, period close…) take effect at once and are logged here with no new version.

methods.name: lock
methods.comment: Serialises every command on a kind (the chain rules compare versions with each other).

methods.name: verify
methods.comment: Public (no sign-in): anyone holding the document can check it. Shows only what is printed on it, masked.

name: org.gcc.usp.platform.identity.AuthController
comment: Sign-in. A platform account (identity.platform_user) is checked first, against its stored hash; any other name is an SAP user (SU01), checked by calling the employee profile service as that user. On success the portal opens an in-memory session: web gets an HttpOnly cookie, mobile a bearer token.

methods.name: changePassword
methods.comment: A platform account changes its own password (required after an administrator set or reset it).

methods.name: session
methods.comment: Who is signed in (the token is not echoed back here).

name: org.gcc.usp.platform.identity.AuthController$SessionView
comment: {@code kind}: sap (employee) or platform (no SAP user); {@code mustChangePassword}: nothing else is allowed until it is changed.

name: org.gcc.usp.platform.identity.CurrentUser
comment: The person behind the current request: an employee (SAP sign-in) or a platform account.

methods.name: personId
methods.comment: Employee number, or {@code u:<username>} for a platform account.

methods.name: hasSap
methods.comment: Signed in with SAP (an employee); platform accounts are not.

methods.name: isPlatformAdmin
methods.comment: Platform administrator: a platform account with the admin flag, or an employee listed in {@code USP_BOOTSTRAP_ADMINS} (first run and recovery; decided at sign-in).

methods.name: sapCredentials
methods.comment: Credentials for calling SAP as this user (SEC-03). A platform account has none: it cannot use SAP-backed features.

name: org.gcc.usp.platform.identity.PasswordChangeGate
comment: A platform account with a temporary password can only change it (and sign out) until it does.

name: org.gcc.usp.platform.identity.PlatformUserController
comment: Platform administrators manage platform accounts (people without an SAP user).

name: org.gcc.usp.platform.identity.PortalSession
comment: A signed-in user, in the backend's memory only. An employee signs in with SAP (SU01) and is identified by the employee number; a platform account (no SAP user) by {@code u:<username>} and never calls SAP.

methods.name: personId
methods.comment: The portal-wide identity: employee number, or {@code u:<username>} for a platform account.

methods.name: employeeNo
methods.comment: Null for platform accounts.

methods.name: credentials
methods.comment: Null for platform accounts.

name: org.gcc.usp.platform.identity.SessionFilter
comment: Authenticates requests carrying a portal session: {@code Authorization: Bearer <token>} (mobile) or the HttpOnly cookie (web).

name: org.gcc.usp.platform.identity.SessionStore
comment: Sessions live in this JVM's memory only (credentials must never reach the database). ponytail: single instance; with several backend instances use sticky sessions or an encrypted shared cache.

methods.name: open
methods.comment: Opens a session; {@code build} receives the new random token.

methods.name: endAll
methods.comment: Signs a platform account out everywhere (disabled, or its password reset by an administrator).

name: org.gcc.usp.platform.org.OrgDirectory
comment: The org structure, read from SAP as the signed-in user (SAP-010 … SAP-014). Lookups are memoised for the current HTTP request only, so a request page or inbox asks SAP once per unit/position; nothing outlives the request.

methods.name: me
methods.comment: SAP-010: the signed-in user's positions.

methods.name: describe
methods.comment: Name and position title for display; falls back to the employee number when SAP does not know the person.

methods.name: isoDate
methods.comment: SAP dates arrive as dd-MM-yyyy or ISO; normalised to ISO.

methods.name: cache
methods.comment: One map per HTTP request (request attribute); null outside a request (scheduler), meaning no memo.
